title: Unity in the body of Christ — Ephesians 4
paragraphs: Unity in the body of Christ — Ephesians 4
They didn’t break the church with a sword.
One wanted the spotlight. Another wanted control. Someone got offended. Someone stopped listening. And suddenly the Body of Christ started fighting itself like it forgot whose Body it was.

That is why Ephesians 4 does not begin with platform.
It begins with posture.

“Walk worthy.”
With humility.
With gentleness.
With patience.
Bearing with one another in love.

That is not weakness.
That is spiritual maturity under pressure.

But here’s what we miss: unity is not pretending we are all the same. Unity is sinners saved by the same Christ, filled by the same Spirit, held together by the same grace. One body. One Spirit. One hope. One Lord. One faith. One baptism. One God and Father of all.

And that means division is never just a personality problem.
It is a Gospel problem.

Because Jesus did not bleed to build isolated believers with private opinions and public bitterness. He gave gifts to the church, called every member to grow, and commanded the Body to build itself up in love. Not in pride. Not in competition. In love.

So if there is envy in your heart, repent.
If there is offense you keep feeding, surrender it.
If there is a brother or sister you have reduced to an enemy, remember the cross.
Christ is not glorified when His Body tears itself apart.
He is glorified when broken people kneel low, forgive deeply, speak truth in love, and grow up into Him.

This is the call of Ephesians 4:
Stop acting like fragments.
Live like one Body.
Under one Head.
Jesus Christ.

And here’s the hope—unity does not start with us trying harder. It starts with Christ changing our hearts. The same Savior who forgives our sin can also kill our pride, heal our wounds, and teach us to love His people again.

Church, come back to the cross.
That is where division dies.
That is where unity begins.
